top_reviews.text: 500 deposit for parking but you get it back. Not a clean or modern apartment-style place. It kind of looks like a prison, but when you make it your own, it works out. It's the definition of “at least you have a head to rest”. You're required to do two hours of labor in order to live here. Labor includes: taking care of plants, cleaning walkways, cleaning elevators, cleaning the laundry room, etc. The CO-OP has 3 sections, which is why we're called the Super Co-op. The first and second floors are Laurel, the third is Nueces, and the fourth and fifth are Halstead. Nueces is the only section of the building where rooms have their own kitchen, and everyone has their own restroom. All the other floors have a communal kitchen, and as part of their labor, they also have to cook for everyone else, depending on what's on the menu. All of it is student ran so there is drama, but we do report to a main office.

top_reviews.text: Walls are thin but amenities are great. It's a greek life apartment so expect it to be loud at nights. Apartment lobby and halls get cleaned daily. Maintenance is slow and there is only 3 elevators for 19 floors. Front desk people are helpful. Deliveries rarely get stolen. If you live next to the trash chute then it smells terrible and overflows on weekends. I live in 2x2 and have the room with no window, but the large layout and space makes up for it.

So many hidden premium fees, elevators ALWAYS broken, the parking garage has been broken for months, the pool is closed at least 3x a month, managers are always gone and never helpful. Only nice thing is that the maintenance guys are so sweet and work very hard to fix everything, there just are way too many people and issues for the 3 of them.

Scoured around the internet! No hidden fees (just read the contract carefully). I really like my experience overall. Only downside is that mold grows and in one particular bathroom, it’s genuinely horrible (the smell, how fast mold grows, etc)

top_reviews.text: Decent apartment. The only downside to living here was in the fall semester when the elevator would go out all the time and we lived on the top floor. They have gotten a new contractor who seems to have really turned things around elevaor wise. It may seem far from campus but the bus stop is right outside your door. Doesn't have a gym of dedicated study rooms (only a little area in the lobby) and I know there are places that go for around the same rate with gyms. Also really nice if you're a cyclist because they have a dedicated bike cage in the parking garage. Plus if you're a dog owner they have their own closed off dog park in the back.

top_reviews.text: $35 a month green fee, great amenities (rooftop pool 30 floors high, gym, yoga room, saunas, cycling room, study area 2nd floor, free printing, Luxer package delivery system, refrigerators in mail room for grocery deliveries), however my first semester here we went down to 2 elevators out of the 4 in the building operational after just a week or two into the Fall semester. Being on the 25th floor made calling for an elevator extremely difficult with long wait times before seeing an elevator. By the time the elevator picked up people from floors 30-20 it was more or less full making people on lower floors have to wait even longer to get in an empty elevator. Additionally at times it would be down to 1 elevator because one of the elevators out of the 2 was getting overworked with the reduced elevator capacity making management slow down that elevator. Eventually they were fixed after 3 months (December) and have been fine ever since but definitely not a good elevator experience the first half of the year.

extremely tiny bedrooms but makes up for it with floor to ceiling windows, large kitchen island with waterfall countertop edge, and tower/campus view. decent amenities and aesthetic study spaces. elevator issues (often gets stuck/sometimes drop several floors). extremely tight parking garage!!!!!! (like every single car has scrapes down the side and it’s pretty difficult to turn the corner without having to reverse)
Green fee, premium floor fee, they charge more if the trash room is overfilled even if it wasn’t you. Thin walls
